name: Atlantic hurricanes
summary: NHC's 12 Nov discussion reports no active Atlantic tropical cyclones; season formally ends on 30 Nov
state: The National Hurricane Center's tropical weather discussion issued at 1215 UTC on 12 Nov reports no active tropical cyclones in the Atlantic, Caribbean or Gulf (NHC). It notes a weak low in the Gulf with no significant winds and a low in the southern Caribbean driving fresh to strong trade winds over the central Caribbean. With no storm threatening land, the signal stays Normal; the season formally ends on 30 Nov.
for_you: No tropical storm currently threatens land. Anyone in or travelling to the Caribbean or US Gulf coast can follow National Hurricane Center outlooks and FCDO travel advice for any late-season change.
rubric_hit: Normal: no hurricane or tropical storm active or threatening land within 5 days (NHC, 12 Nov)

sources.title: NOAA National Hurricane Center — Tropical Weather Discussion, Atlantic, 1215 UTC 12 Nov

why: Atlantic hurricanes hit the US Gulf coast, Caribbean and Central America — and refinery and insurance markets with them.
drivers: Sea-surface temperatures, ENSO, wind shear, season timing (Jun–Nov peak Aug–Oct).
